key_insight: Affine functional multipliers make distributionally robust data fusion scalable while providing upper bounds tighter than aggregation-based relaxations.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports robust decisions and neural network training using fragmented evidence without collapsing distinct sources into one ambiguity set.
method: Represent each evidence source by an ambiguity set and optimize against their intersection.
Couple sets through functional Lagrange multipliers, then restrict these to affine decision rules for decomposable upper bounds.
Use finite conic reformulations in special cases or subgradient methods for weakly convex losses.
evidence_signal: Portfolio, newsvendor, and binary classification experiments report near-exact values where computable, better scaling than exact methods, and stronger out-of-sample performance than aggregation benchmarks.
watch_item: Affine bounds are not generally exact; exactness is established for quadratic losses over Wasserstein balls around Gaussian references.
paper_title: Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization
